judgment.reasoning_summary: The problem is a classic application of the pigeonhole principle. For any set of n distinct positive integers, the sums of all possible non-empty subsets form a sequence of sums. Since there are 2^n - 1 such subsets, and each sum modulo n can take on n possible values (0 through n-1), by the pigeonhole principle, at least two of these sums must be congruent modulo n. The difference between these two sums is a subset sum that is divisible by n. Therefore, the smallest n for which this property holds is 2, as any set of 2 distinct positive integers will have a subset sum divisible by 2.
